name: can compose unrelated changes
scenario: composeDesc of '5 0:2' (insert 2 at the end of a 5-length document) then '1 2:0 4' (delete 2 at 1).
class_reason: Pure state values (change descriptions, change sets, Text, selections); no layout, grammar or DOM.
port_notes: Helper `mk(spec)` (mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-change.ts:4-12): repeatedly matches /^(\d+)(?::(\d+))?\s*/ at the start of the remaining string; each match pushes two numbers: +group1 (length) and +group2 when present, else -1 (so "5" is an unchanged span of 5, "0:2" an insertion of 2, "2:0" a deletion of 2, "2:3" a replacement); an empty string gives no sections; a string that does not match makes `exec` return null and the helper throw a TypeError. It builds the value with the protected constructor (`new (ChangeDesc as any)(sections)`), bypassing every check (open question Q5); the same array is obtainable through ChangeDesc.fromJSON. Assertions compare `String(desc)`, i.e. the @internal ChangeDesc.toString format (len or len:ins joined by single spaces), with `ist` (strict ===). Helper `comp(...specs)` (test-change.ts:34-37): pops the last argument as the expected string, maps the rest through `mk`, folds them left to right with `composeDesc`, and asserts `String(result) === expected`. Positions are plain counts; no text, so D1 and D2 do not change any value.
